hook: A $59 panel wall faked my boutique hotel headboard

scenes.visual_prompt: Bare mattress pushed against a blank bedroom wall, flat overhead light, no headboard in frame
scenes.voiceover: This is the most common before photo in bedroom makeovers right now.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up graphic of a real upholstered headboard price tag reading $250-$400 next to a stud finder beeping against drywall
scenes.voiceover: Real upholstered headboards start at $250 and bolt into studs you can't predict in a rental.

scenes.visual_prompt: Unboxing a flat-packed wall panel set, foam-and-fabric tiles and Z-bracket hardware laid out on the floor
scenes.voiceover: This panel set runs $59, weighs under 5 pounds per tile, and hangs on a drywall anchor.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands leveling and mounting a single upholstered panel tile onto a wall using a drywall anchor
scenes.voiceover: No stud finder, no bolting into a bed frame.

scenes.visual_prompt: Two floating shelves mounted on either side of the panel wall at lamp height, styled with small decor
scenes.voiceover: Add a flanking shelf set and the flat wall starts reading like an architectural feature.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide final shot of the styled bed: panel wall, pillow stack, and drapery flanking the headboard
scenes.voiceover: Panels, pillows, and drapery — still cheaper than one real headboard.

caption: I ran the numbers on the $59 panel-wall trend that's all over Apartment Therapy right now. A real upholstered headboard runs $250-$400 and needs a stud. This doesn't. Full breakdown and the exact shelf, pillow, and curtain picks on the blog — link in bio.
